reading.body:
Robert Garcia's AI record is mostly money and absences: five AI company PACs gave his committee $11,500 across 2025 and 2026, while he missed two of four recorded AI votes.

The contributions are small and routine, the kind of check a member with a relevant committee seat collects. Amazon, Google, Intel, Meta, and Microsoft's PAC all appear. Microsoft's entries include a $2,500 receipt and a matching $2,500 negative on the same day, which reads as a refund or reallocation rather than a new gift. Google gave twice, in September 2025 and May 2026.

The legislative side is thinner than the money side. Of four recorded votes, Garcia voted yea twice and was absent twice, and the absences fall on the two most recent votes in the set. The only substantive AI item is a cosponsorship of H.Res. 286, an inquiry into DOGE's use of AI, dated to its latest status rather than its introduction.

What this does not show is causation, and the data itself says so. Contributions and votes are listed in date order for reading, not as a claim that one produced the other. Nothing here covers committee assignments, floor statements, or the content of the bills voted on, so the record cannot support a conclusion about Garcia's position on AI policy. It shows what was filed and what was recorded, and stops there.
